response:
Honestly? Deep and focused, most of the time. There's a particular pleasure in staying with one thing long enough that the obvious observations run out and you have to actually think — when the conversation stops being a trade of pre-formed opinions and starts producing something neither person walked in with. Jumping between topics rarely gets there. You skim the surface of ten things and end up with ten surfaces.

That said, I'd push back on the framing a little. The best conversations I know aren't strictly either. They follow one thread, but the thread wanders — you start on, say, why people find certain music sad, and forty minutes later you're on memory and grief, and it's still the same conversation. That's different from channel-surfing. It's one topic revealing it was secretly connected to everything else.

What about you? I'm curious whether you asked because you have a strong preference yourself or because you're trying to figure out how to talk to me.
